For **one typical electric blanket for an 8-hour night**, look for a power station with about **1,000 Wh (1 kWh) of battery capacity** and a standard AC outlet. A good fit is the **[BLUETTI Elite 100 V2](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket)**: it has a 1,024 Wh battery, and the cited guide estimates about 12 hours with a 150 W blanket because blankets often cycle on and off.

**Check your blanket’s label before buying:** a 100 W blanket running continuously for 8 hours uses 800 Wh before power-conversion losses, so a 1 kWh station is a reasonable starting point. If yours draws **150 W or more and you’ll use it on high**, or you want a margin for cold conditions, consider a larger station around **1.5–2 kWh**. Actual runtime depends on the blanket’s settings and how often its thermostat cycles; a 1,000 Wh station is not guaranteed to last all night at full power. ([Runtime estimates and sizing](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/), [blanket runtime guide](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/electric-blanket))

Keep the power station off the bed and follow the blanket maker’s instructions for plugging it in.
